About Hermia

It was never about the leads. It was about knowing the job first.

Hermia stands between an incoming enquiry and your team's next move. It replies within about a minute, asks the questions your business would ask, checks every answer, and hands your team work that is ready to act on, whatever your industry. Nobody chases, nobody guesses, nobody retypes.

See how it works Why we built it
Why we do what we do

Most businesses don't have a lead problem. They have a detail problem.

Enquiries aren't the hard part. Most businesses get plenty. What arrives is a sentence: “leak in the kitchen”, “the heater's not working”, “can I book in?”, “I want to make a claim”.

A sentence isn't something your team can act on. Before anyone moves, they need what sits behind it: where, how urgent, who is involved, what has already happened and what the customer can show.

Without that detail, the office chases, the next person guesses, and the customer tells the same story to three different people. The work is slower, the margins are thinner, and the business looks less organised than it really is.

Hermia exists to close that gap before anyone moves. It doesn't generate leads and it doesn't just reply to them. It takes responsibility for the first conversation until your team has a real starting point.

The same gap, in every industry.

What the enquiry says, and what your team actually needs before it can act.

Trades and field services

“Leak in the kitchen.”

The address, access, how urgent it is, photos, and who is paying.

Real estate

“Can we inspect on Saturday?”

Which listing, buying or renting, where their finance is up to, and when they can inspect.

Property management

“The heater's not working.”

Which property, when the tenant is home, how to get in, and any pets.

Legal and professional services

“I need help with a contract.”

The type of matter, the deadline, the other party, and the documents.

Clinics and healthcare admin

“Can I book in?”

The kind of appointment, a preferred time, any referral, and how they'll pay.

Insurance

“I want to make a claim.”

What happened and when, the policy, and photos of the damage.

Finance, lending and banking

“I'd like to talk about a home loan.”

Taken from the email and saved straight into your CRM: who's asking, what it's about and how to reach them. No messages are sent to your customers.

Car dealers

“Is this car still available?”

Which car, any trade-in, finance, and when they can come in for a test drive.

Education and training

“Can I still enrol for February?”

The course, the intake, how they want to study, and what they need to know first.

Hospitality

“A table for 8 on Friday?”

Menus, specials and function packages change every week. Hermia answers from your latest notes and takes the booking (coming soon).

Every business asks its own questions, in its own words. The questions change from industry to industry. The standard doesn't.

And then there's the CRM

A CRM is only as good as what goes into it.

The detail problem doesn't end with the enquiry. It ends up in the CRM: the same customer saved three times, half-empty records, notes that say “see email” or “call back??”, and the real details stuck in an inbox or in someone's head. Nobody trusts it, so nobody uses it properly.

Hermia stops the mess at the door. Everything it puts into your CRM arrives complete, in the right place, once.

  • One enquiry, one record.The same enquiry sent twice, or a customer writing on two channels, becomes one record, not three.
  • Every answer in its place.Each answer lands in the description or the notes, wherever you chose, one answer per line.
  • No silent blanks.If something wasn't answered, the record says so: Not answered (asked 3 times).
  • Photos with the record.Checked first, then kept with the enquiry they belong to.
  • Nothing retyped.No copying from chats and no re-keying from emails.
  • Works with what you use.Hermia writes into the system your team already works in. If yours isn't connected yet, every prepared enquiry still reaches you straight away as a secure lead docket by email.

Setup

You decide what “prepared” means.

No two operations define a ready job the same way. Before Hermia speaks to a single customer, your business tells it what a complete enquiry looks like.

Your standard, not ours.

Why it matters to your operation

A generic checklist produces generic jobs. When the questions come from your operation, the brief that arrives already matches the way your team works. The office stops translating and starts scheduling.

What you set

  1. The channels your enquiries arrive on, and the channel you want customers answered on.
  2. Your industry or trade, so the standard questions match the work you actually do.
  3. Your own questions, up to 35, in your own words. For each one you choose where the answer belongs: the job description or the internal notes.
  4. How the next step works: an estimate drawn from your own price list, or a simple yes or no confirmation.
  5. Who is told when a lead is ready, by email.

Intake

One customer. One record.

The same enquiry often arrives twice: a form submitted again, an email forwarded, a customer who writes on two channels. Hermia makes sure it becomes one job.

One story per customer.

Why it matters to your operation

What happens

  1. An identical enquiry arriving again is recognised and removed before anything else happens.

Conversation

A reply before they call someone else.

The first business to respond clearly is usually the one that gets the job. Hermia replies on the customer's own channel, as the assistant for your business.

No enquiry waits for business hours.

Why it matters to your operation

An enquiry that arrives at 9pm is answered at 9pm. Your team keeps working, and the customer knows they have been heard before they think of calling anyone else.

What happens

  1. Within about a minute, the customer hears from Hermia, introduced as the digital assistant for your business.
  2. The first question is the one that matters most: how urgent is it? Emergency: needs assistance today, Urgent: within 2 to 4 days or Standard: this week is fine.
  3. If the customer's number can't receive WhatsApp, the same first message reaches them by email, with the same choices one tap away.
  4. Every customer can reply STOP to opt out at any time.

Conversation

The right questions, asked properly.

Hermia asks what your team needs to know: the standard questions for your kind of work, then your own. One at a time, in plain language.

One question at a time, until it's answered.

Why it matters to your operation

Your team stops making the call it always makes (“what's the gate code?”, “when is settlement?”) because the question was asked and answered before anyone picked up the phone.

What happens

  1. Every enquiry starts with how urgent it is. For trades, the standard questions for the work follow: the problem, the site, access, safety, timing and who is paying.
  2. Your own questions follow, in the order you set.
  3. Every new question is reviewed once when you add it. Spelling and grammar are tidied without changing the meaning, and a question that is too vague to answer is flagged to you.
  4. If an answer isn't usable, the question is asked again with an example of a good answer.
  5. You can change your questions whenever you need to. The change applies from the customer's next reply, and conversations already underway carry on without a hitch.

Accuracy

Nothing guessed. Nothing invented.

Whether an answer is good enough is never left to a single opinion. Hermia's tone is warm, but its standard does not move.

An honest gap beats a confident guess.

Why it matters to your operation

Your team can trust the brief. When something is missing, the brief says so, instead of looking complete and turning out to be wrong later.

What happens

  1. Every answer is judged by two independent reviewers. It counts only when both agree it is genuinely useful. If one is unavailable, another takes its place.
  2. OK is not an answer to a question that asks for a fact, and neither is a string of random letters. Both are asked again.
  3. A customer who still can't answer after three attempts is moved on politely, and the record says exactly that: Not answered (asked 3 times). Urgency is never assumed.
  4. Every message Hermia writes is checked before it is sent: no times it can't keep, no promises, and no prices or links unless they're your own, written in your notes, nothing longer than a short reply. A message that fails the check is replaced by the plain question.
  5. Nothing is filled in on the customer's behalf. If they didn't say it or show it, it isn't in the brief.

Accuracy

Photos that belong to the job.

A photo can save a visit or a phone call, or waste one. Hermia checks every image the moment it arrives.

Evidence, not attachments.

Why it matters to your operation

Your people see the actual problem before they act, and your staff never have to open something they shouldn't.

What happens

  1. Photos and videos are checked against the enquiry before they are saved or passed on.
  2. Unrelated or inappropriate images never reach your team. The customer is asked, politely, for a clear photo of what they need help with.
  3. Several photos sent at once receive one reply, not several.
  4. Accepted photos and videos stay with the same job, so your team sees the problem rather than reading about it.

Conversation

One follow-up. Never a nag.

People get busy. An enquiry that goes quiet isn't always lost. Often it only needs one reminder: It's Hermia from your business again. Just checking in on your enquiry. Do you still need help?

Once, at the right time.

Why it matters to your operation

Work that would have gone quietly cold is recovered, without making your business look desperate or pushy.

What happens

  1. If a new customer hasn't replied after 24 hours, Hermia sends one friendly follow-up, on WhatsApp or by email, wherever the conversation started.
  2. It only goes out between 9am and 7pm in your business's own time zone. Never at midnight.
  3. It is cancelled the moment the customer replies, and never sent for an enquiry that is closed or more than three days old.
  4. There is never a second one.

Handover

A brief your team can act on.

When the conversation is complete, what arrives isn't a chat log. It's a prepared job.

Nothing is handed over half-finished.

Why it matters to your operation

No retyping, no copying from a chat, no “what did they say about access?”. The office acts, and whoever goes next arrives prepared.

What arrives

  1. The enquiry goes straight into the system your team already works in, your CRM or job management system, with the description and notes already written and every answer to your own questions on its own line.
  2. A private lead docket is emailed to the people you chose, including the answers to your own questions.
  3. System not connected yet? Every prepared enquiry still reaches you straight away as the lead docket by email. And if a delivery to your system can't be confirmed within 30 minutes, the full brief is emailed to you instead. Nothing is lost.

Reliability

Busy days don't drop enquiries.

The day your phone runs hot is the day the system matters most. Hermia is built to slow down gracefully, never to drop work.

Slow down, never drop.

Why it matters to your operation

Your busiest week (a storm, a heatwave, the end of financial year) should be your best week, not the week enquiries go missing.

What happens

  1. When a messaging channel asks Hermia to slow down, messages wait their turn and go out within minutes. They are never thrown away, and never swapped for something less suitable.
  2. Enquiries arriving in a rush are queued and handled in order.
  3. Every check has a backup. If one reviewer is unavailable, another takes its place; if nothing can check an answer, the answer waits rather than slipping through unchecked.
  4. Anything that fails is tried again automatically, and our team is alerted the moment something needs a person.

Trust

What Hermia will never do.

Hermia prepares the work. Qualified people make the decisions. Those lines don't blur.

Prepare the work. Never pretend to be the expert.

Why it matters to your operation

Automation that oversteps creates more work than it saves. Your team can rely on Hermia precisely because it knows where to stop.

The lines we hold

  • No final prices. Estimates come only from your own price list, and anything uncertain goes to your team instead of being guessed.
  • No expert judgement. Hermia never makes safety assessments, never gives legal, medical or financial advice, and never stands in for licensed or regulated work.
  • No promises it can't keep. It never offers a time your team hasn't got.
  • No pretending. An unanswered question is recorded as unanswered.
  • No taking your customer. Hermia speaks for your business, and the relationship stays yours.
  • No holding on. A customer who replies STOP is not contacted again.
